drug-affinity-complex.definition: A chemical hook added to a peptide so that it bonds to albumin, a protein in the blood. It was designed to keep the peptide in the blood for days.

maleimide.definition: A small, reactive ring of atoms. It forms a lasting bond with a sulfur group on proteins such as albumin.

covalent-bond.definition: A strong chemical bond in which two atoms share electrons. Unlike loose binding, it does not simply let go again.

mod-grf.definition: A lab-made peptide of 29 amino acids, based on the first part of the hormone GHRH. It is the CJC-1295 chain without the drug affinity complex, and no study in people has been published.

trough-level.definition: The lowest level of a hormone or medicine in the blood, between its peaks.

hyperplasia.definition: Growth of a tissue because its cells multiply. It is not cancer, but it can make an organ larger than normal.

comet-assay.definition: A lab test for broken DNA in single cells. Under the microscope, damaged DNA trails behind the cell like the tail of a comet.

flushing.definition: Sudden redness and warmth of the face, neck or chest, because small blood vessels in the skin widen. It can come with a short drop in blood pressure.

trifluoroacetate-salt.definition: A salt form of a peptide made with trifluoroacetic acid, often left over from lab synthesis. It is a different substance from the free base or the acetate salt.
